title: Transaction
description:
The only writable object in the system, and the thing everything else is derived from. APPEND-ONLY: a correction is a new reversing row, never an edit. Source of truth: docs/DATA_MODEL.md, table `transaction`.

ENCODING RULE: money and quantity are JSON strings, never numbers, so no precision is lost in transit and no consumer is tempted to parse them into a binary floating-point type. Rates (see performance.schema.json) are the sole exception.

account_id.description: Which demat/broker account. Absent in engine unit fixtures, which test pure calculation.

isin.description: THE identity of a security. 12 characters; INE.../INF... are the common prefixes. Never key on ticker: tickers get renamed and reused, ISINs do not.

txn_date.description: TRADE date, not settlement date. Reconciliation depends on this distinction.

txn_type.description: Quantity and cash effects per txn_type are tabulated in docs/DATA_MODEL.md and docs/ENGINE_SPEC.md section 1.

quantity.description: ALWAYS POSITIVE. Direction comes from txn_type, never from a sign here.

charges.description: Brokerage + STT + GST + stamp, combined. Defaults to 0.

dividend_amount.description: Used only when txn_type is DIVIDEND, where quantity and price are 0. A separate field rather than overloading `price`, because a dividend is a per-holding cash event, not a per-unit trade.

source.description: Which adapter produced this row. The engine must never branch on it.

source_ref.description: Contract-note number, trade id, or equivalent from the originating document.

dedupe_key.description: sha256(account_id | source | source_ref | isin | txn_date | txn_type | quantity | price). A UNIQUE INDEX on this column is what makes re-importing safe. Email forwarding will deliver the same contract note twice; the database must be the thing that refuses it, not application code someone later forgets to call.

raw_payload.description: The original parsed row, kept for forensics.

decimal.description: An exact decimal carried as a string. Maps to Python decimal.Decimal and Postgres NUMERIC(20,6).
